result.builder:
Goal: make packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js accept several files and stdin, for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104. Open one pull request.

Context: packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js takes one file at the moment (process.argv[2]). It reads the file, calls lint(text) from packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js and prints `<file>:<line>: <error>` for each bad row, replacing newlines in the error with spaces. Exit codes are 0 for clean, 1 for bad rows and 2 for usage or read errors. The tests are in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js and use node:test. They spawn the bin with spawnSync.

Steps:
1. Do not touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js. lint(text) must stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. Rewrite packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js so it does the following (plain ES modules, no dependencies):
   - Take every argument in process.argv.slice(2).
   - No arguments: write a usage line to stderr, for example `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]` (mention that `-` means stdin), and exit 2.
   - More than one `-` argument: write a usage error to stderr and exit 2. Do this check before reading anything.
   - Otherwise go through the arguments in the order given. For `-`, read stdin with readFileSync(0, 'utf8') and label it `-`. For any other argument, call readFileSync(arg, 'utf8') and use the argument exactly as given for the label.
   - If a read fails, write `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` to stderr, note the failure and go on to the next file. Do not exit early.
   - For each file that reads, print `<label>:<line>: <error>` lines to stdout in file order, then in row order, in the same format as now (newlines in the error become spaces).
   - Exit status: 2 if any file could not be read; otherwise 1 if any row in any file was bad; otherwise 0.
   - Keep the behaviour for one file the same as before, so the existing tests still pass.
3. Add node:test tests in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (you may also use a new test file under packages/jsonl-lint/test/). Use the existing spawnSync helper and pass `input` for stdin. Cover each case:
   - two clean files: exit 0, no stdout
   - one bad file among several clean ones: exit 1, only that file's lines with its name as the prefix
   - stdin via `-` with clean input (exit 0) and with bad input (exit 1, lines prefixed `-:`)
   - a missing file among good ones: exit 2, stderr names the missing file, and the other files are still checked and reported (include a bad file so its lines still appear on stdout)
   - two `-` arguments: exit 2 with an error on stderr
   - no arguments: exit 2 with usage on stderr
   Keep the existing tests.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md:
   - Usage becomes `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`.
   - Say that `-` reads stdin, is reported as `-`, and may appear only once.
   - Say that files are checked in order.
   - State the exit codes: 0 when every file is clean; 1 when any row in any file is bad; 2 when no file is named, `-` is given twice, or any file can't be read (error on stderr, the other files are still checked).
5. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make sure it passes.
6. Commit, push and open one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test. The PR body must contain the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to run on the PR head, and fix anything that fails until it is green.
result.verifier:
Check out the pull request's head and run every check from the repository root. Make a scratch directory, for example `T=$(mktemp -d)`, holding:
- `$T/a.jsonl` containing `{"a":1}\n`
- `$T/b.jsonl` containing `{"b":2}\n`
- `$T/bad.jsonl` containing `{"x":1}\n{oops}\n`

B below means `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js`.

Check 1. Expect line: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before".
Run `B $T/bad.jsonl $T/a.jsonl $T/bad.jsonl` and also `B $T/bad.jsonl` on its own.
- PASS: every file named is checked. Each bad row produces one stdout line of the form `<file>:<line>: <error>`, with the file argument as given. The lines appear in the order the files were named. A file named twice is reported twice. The single-file output is in the same format as before (`$T/bad.jsonl:2: <JSON.parse message>`).
- FAIL: a named file is skipped, the lines are out of argument order, or the format differs from that.

Check 2. Expect line: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)".
Run `printf '{oops}\n' | B $T/a.jsonl -`, then `printf '{"ok":1}\n' | B -`, then `printf '{}\n' | B - -; echo $?`.
- PASS: the first prints a line starting `-:1: `. The second prints nothing about a bad row. The third exits with status 2.
- FAIL: stdin is not read, it is labelled anything other than `-`, or `- -` does not exit 2.

Check 3. Expect line: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)".
Run these and record each exit status, stdout and stderr:
- `B $T/a.jsonl $T/b.jsonl`
- `B $T/a.jsonl $T/bad.jsonl $T/b.jsonl`
- `B`
- `B $T/a.jsonl $T/missing.jsonl $T/bad.jsonl`
PASS: the statuses are 0, 1, 2 and 2. In the last run, stderr has an error, and stdout still contains the bad-row lines for `$T/bad.jsonl`, which shows the other files were checked and reported. FAIL: any status differs, the last run has no stderr error, or the last run stops before reporting `$T/bad.jsonl`.

Check 4. Expect line: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged".
Run `git diff <merge-base with main>..HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js` (find the merge base with `git merge-base origin/main HEAD`).
- PASS: the lint function's code and behaviour are unchanged (an empty diff is the clear pass).
- FAIL: lint's signature, body or behaviour changed.

Check 5. Expect line: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage".
Run `npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint`, then read the test files under packages/jsonl-lint/test/ and packages/jsonl-lint/README.md.
- PASS: the tests run under node:test and pass, and between them there are tests for all of these cases: two clean files; one bad file among several; stdin via `-` with clean input; stdin via `-` with bad input; a missing file among good ones; two `-` arguments; no arguments. The README documents the multi-file usage, including `-` for stdin.
- FAIL: any case has no test, the tests fail, or the README does not document the new usage.

Check 6. Expect line: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head".
Run `gh pr view <pr> --repo suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test --json body,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` and `npm test` at the repository root.
- PASS: there is one PR on that repo with the change. Its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Root `npm test` passes. The `test` workflow check at the head commit has concluded success.
- FAIL: the body lacks that line, `npm test` fails, or the test workflow is not successful at the head.

Advisory (not pass/fail):
- Check that stderr for `- -` and for no arguments contains a usage message.
- Check that the `-` usage error is raised before any file is read.
- Check that the order of stdout lines inside one file follows row order.
- Run the existing single-file tests in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js to confirm nothing regressed.

text:
I wrote both briefs for issue #104 and the harness accepted them, so they can't be changed now. I made no changes to the repository.

**Builder brief:**
- **CLI:** rewrite `packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js` to take any number of files in order. `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`.
- **Errors and exit codes:**
  - No arguments, or `-` given twice, is a usage error with exit 2.
  - A file that can't be read gets an error on stderr, and the other files are still checked.
  - The exit status is 2 if any file can't be read, otherwise 1 if any row is bad, otherwise 0.
- **Unchanged:** `lint(text)` in `src/index.js` stays exactly as it is, and output for a single file looks the same as before.
- **Tests and README:** add `node:test` tests for each case the issue lists and update the package README.
- **PR:** open one PR whose body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, and get `npm test` and the test workflow green at its head.

**Verifier brief:** six checks, one per acceptance line and in the same order. Each runs real commands at the PR head against small test files: the CLI with several files, stdin, a missing file and no arguments, plus a diff of `src/index.js`, `npm test`, and the PR body and workflow status read with `gh`.

**Where I filled gaps in the issue:**
- **Exit code with both kinds of failure:** the issue doesn't say what to return when one file can't be read and another has bad rows. I told the builder to return 2 in that case.
- **When to reject a second `-`:** I told the builder to reject it before reading any file. The verifier only checks for exit 2, because that's all the issue requires.
- **Advisory checks:** stricter checks the issue doesn't require went under an Advisory heading so they can't fail the PR. These are a usage message on stderr, row order within one file, and the existing single-file tests still passing.
